messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] rhwrite(list(1,2,3),"/tmp/x") Fails
parts:
Aah, i think you have an old version or I haven't pushed the new version.

Just to verify, type rhwrite at the prompt to see the source, Do  you see this(below)
i.e rhoptions()$mropts[[1]]  or you can try typing rhoptions()$mropts[[1]] and see if mapred.map.tasks is not null

A quick fix is specify the value of N, it is the number of files the elements of list to written to.

function (lo, dest, N = NULL) 
{
    if (!is.list(lo)) 
        stop("lo must be a list")
    namv <- names(lo)
    if (is.null(N)) {
  --->>>      x1 <- rhoptions()$mropts[[1]]$mapred.map.tasks  ### THIS LINE
   --->>>     x2 <- rhoptions()$mropts[[1]]$mapred.tasktracker.map.tasks.maximum  ## THIS LINE
        N <- as.numeric(x1) * as.numeric(x2)

}
    if (is.null(N) || N == 0 || N > length(lo)) 
        N <- length(lo)

....

parts:
Hi,

A) I dont see mapred.map.tasks or mapred.tasktracker.map.tasks.maximum.
I've made a fix to the rhwrite code that defaults N to 1 both of these files are missing.
 
B)  What option in Hadoop creates _SUCCESS? I wrote rhread to ignore _logs but this one is new to me.
Quick fix:

rhread('/tmp/test/p*')

Cheers
Joy

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: rhwrite(list(1,2,3),"/tmp/x") Fails
parts: Good post. Also, did you try changing

rhex(rhmr(ifolder = c("/tmp/inout1/"), ofolder = "/tmp/out1", map =
expression(rhcollect(map.keys[[1]], map.values[[1]]))))

to

rhex(rhmr(ifolder = c("/tmp/inout1/p*"), ofolder = "/tmp/out1", map =
expression(rhcollect(map.keys[[1]], map.values[[1]]))))

You can also manually give the files themselves i.e.
ifolder=grep("^part",rhls("/tmp/inout1/")$files,value=TRUE)

Cheers

S

The question is: what is the right way? Currently, the code looks like:

ifolder = switch(inout[1], map = {
flagclz = "sequence"
uu = unclass(rhls(ifolder, rec = TRUE)["file"])$file
uu[grep("data$", uu)]
}, sequence = {
a <- rhls(ifolder, rec = TRUE)$file
}, text = {
rhls(ifolder)$file
})

No special code to 'pick out p*' files, the reason is so that users
who have files not starting with p don't get errors (which is a
possibility with hadoop though rare I guess)

Saptarshi
